newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN investigator urges Rwanda, Zaire end conflict.
newsitem.headline: UN investigator urges Rwanda, Zaire end conflict.

text.p: A U.N. human rights investigator just back from Zaire where hundreds of thousands of refugees are fleeing ethnic clashes urged the leaders of Rwanda and Zaire on Saturday to try to stop the escalating conflict.

Chilean human rights investigator Robert Garreto made the appeal following a visit on October 13-25 to Zaire's capital Kinshasa and its troubled east where 300,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees are fleeing ethnic conflict.

The fighting pits ethnic Tutsis, who have lived in Zaire since the 18th century, against the Zairean army, which says Rwanda is helping the Tutsis. The U.N. fears it could spread with the help of Tutsi-dominated armies in Burundi and Rwanda.

A U.N. statement in Geneva said Garreto was appealing to "the authorities -- Rwandans, Burundians and Zaireans -- to refrain from all acts and declarations that aggrevate an escalation of deadly violence and confrontation."

The statement added Zairean authorities had informed Garreto of evidence that armed Rwandan and Burundian groups were taking part in violence in Zaire with the knowledge of their governments but gave no details.

Following an earlier visit in July to eastern Zaire, Garreto had warned of looming disaster in the volatile region where ethnic tensions worsened after the arrival of a million Rwandan Hutu refugees after 1994's genocide of Tutsis.
In a report released on October 11, he said the conflict was partly due to incitement by Zairean officials.

The latest flare-up comes at a time when Zaire's president Mobutu Sese Seko has been undergoing cancer treatment in Switzerland since August. Mobutu's prolonged absence has raised fears about what will happen in his vast, central African nation if he dies.
